title: Field-level Humanitarian Entrepreneurial Incubators: A How-to Guide
html:
Two years ago, I read a TechCrunch article with interest: Holy Tech Batman! — Can The European Commission Be A Startup Super Hero? [PDF]. Essentially, could the European Commission put in place a more-enabling environment for entrepreneurial efforts. Their first steps had been taken by drafting the Entrepreneurship 2020 Action Plan [PDF].

The TechCrunch post got me thinking: could field-based humanitarian organizations help foster an environment where humanitarian entrepreneurs could flourish? Sure, several international organizations had started their own innovation teams or strategies. But, upon examination, they were all located at headquarters or in development-minded locations. Nothing seemed to be at the front lines of a humanitarian crisis. And, it was very rare to find an instance where an organization “housed” an entrepreneur or was in an ideal geographical location like the Philippines.

This past summer, I was joined by Katie Whipkey. She undertook much more in depth research and confirmed my suspicions. She found a lot of great materials, suggestions and lessons learned during her efforts. So, we decided to turn her findings into guidance for those who are interested in establishing a humanitarian entrepreneurial innovation space at the front lines of a humanitarian response.

[PDF 1 MB]

Our work resulted in the recommendation of creating Humanitarian Entrepreneurial Incubators (HEI) - essentially partnerships between humanitarian organisations and humanitarian entrepreneurs where organisations host entrepreneurs within their office and provide resources and insight to them as they develop and implement an innovative product or service related to humanitarian response. This approach departs from a traditional incubator as it enables deeper collaboration between humanitarian entrepreneurs and organisation staff. We believe that this model could not only spur but truly help scale humanitarian innovation across a response.

So, whether you are looking for a checklist on how to setup an HEI, understand benefits to organizations and entrepreneurs in such a model, determine how to find ideal matches for such a partnership, explore different innovation space types, or read lessons learned from others, we hope that you find the document as inspiring.

Andrej
